title: One direction, or round and about

blocks.text: Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction, e.g.:

items: Мы идём в библиотеку.
We are headed to the library.
Я шла на работу.
I was on my way to work.
Птицы летят на юг.
The birds are flying south.

blocks.text: Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.

items: Ребёнок ходит шесть месяцев.
The child has been walking for six months.
Птицы летают, рыбы плавают, а собаки ходят.
Birds fly, fish swim, and dogs walk.
Мы ходили по городу весь день.
We walked around the city all day.
Она ходит в супермаркет каждую неделю.
She goes to the supermarket every week.
В прошлом году я ездил в Россию.
I went to Russia (and returned) last year.

blocks.text: The basic meaning of the verbs идти, ехать, лететь is being actually on the way to some place: Мы идём в кино. Мы едем в город. Мы летим в Нью-Йорк. — right now.

items: Мы встретили его, когда он шёл в школу.
We met him when he was walking (on his way) to school.
Они каждый день ходили в клуб.
They went to the club every day. (Repeated action.)
Она пошла в библиотеку.
She went to (left for) the library.

blocks.text: Note — that the English "went" is commonly rendered in Russian by either: a) ходил (for the repeated action) or b) пошёл (for the single perfective action).
ходил and ездил instead of был

The verbs "ходил" and "ездил" are sometimes used instead of the verb "был". When so used, "ходил" and "ездил" may indicate a single completed trip (going to and coming from a place). This use is possible in the past tense only.

items: Вы были на почте?
Have you been at the post office?
Да, я ходил (ездил) туда утром.
Yes, I went there in the morning.

blocks.text: Like the verb "ходить" (по комнате) the verb "летать" may be used to indicate motion without a definite goal. Note. — Do not confuse the following: Самолёт летает над городом. (motion without a definite goal) — Самолёт летит над городом. (motion towards a definite goal) — both: The aircraft is flying over the city.

items: Студент ходит по комнате.
The student walks about the room.
Самолёт летает над городом.
The aircraft is flying over the city.

blocks.text: The verb "летал" (like the verbs "ходил" and "ездил") is sometimes used instead of the verb "был". When so used, "летал" may indicate a single completed trip. This use is possible in the past tense only: Вы были в Москве? — Да, я летал туда месяц тому назад.

items: Я буду идти медленно (долго, 2 часа).
I shall be walking slowly (for a long time, for 2 hours) (action in its progress).
Зимой мы часто будем ходить в театр.
In winter we shall often go to the theater. (Repeated action.)
После завтрака они пойдут в магазин.
After breakfast they will go to (leave for) the store.

blocks.text: Note — that the form "буду идти" is seldom used. It occurs mostly when the duration or manner of the action is described. A single action in the future tense is commonly rendered by — "я пойду".

exercises.why: **ездить** (the infinitive) (to go (by horse or vehicle), to ride, to drive) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **ехать** for one direction. — Wiktionary, «ездить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The present tense of all Russian verbs has a twofold function; it indicates: A. an action in progress ("actual" function); B. a repeated or habitual action ("repeated" function). However each action of going (to go on foot, to ride, to fly) is expressed in Russian by two parallel verbs: one for the function A — being on the way to … — иду, еду, лечу; another for the function B — usually, often, etc. to go to … (the motion to and from is understood) — хожу, езжу, летаю.» — DLI, Lesson 22.  «Ходить, ездить: these two verbs belong to the 2nd (И) type of conjugation. Notice that the consonant д changes into ж in the first person singular (like видеть — вижу — видишь).» — DLI, Lesson 22.  «по льду» — movement in various directions, not towards one goal.  Compare: «В прошлом году я ездил в Россию.» (I went to Russia (and returned) last year.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Да, я ходил (ездил) туда утром.» (Yes, I went there in the morning.) — DLI, Lesson 54.  The other choice: **ехать** is from **ехать**, the one-direction verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite). (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Я ___ (лететь — to fly, one way) над облаками.
exercises.why: **летела** is the past tense (feminine) of **лететь** (to fly, to be flying) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **летать** for many directions. past: он лете́л · она лете́ла · оно лете́ло · они лете́ли. — Wiktionary, «лететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The basic meaning of the verbs идти, ехать, лететь is being actually on the way to some place: Мы идём в кино. Мы едем в город. Мы летим в Нью-Йорк. — right now.» — DLI, Lesson 20.  «Лететь: this verb belongs to the 2nd (И) type of conjugation. Notice that т changes into ч in the first person singular.» — DLI, Lessons 19–20.  Compare: «Капитан летит в Вашингтон.» · «Он иногда летает в Вашингтон.» — DLI, Lesson 22. «Птицы летят на юг.» (The birds are flying south.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Пара ___ (идти — to go, walk, one way) рука об руку.
exercises.why: **шла** is the past tense (feminine) of **идти** (to go) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **ходить** for many directions. past: он шёл · она шла́ · оно шло́ · они шли́. — Wiktionary, «идти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The basic meaning of the verbs идти, ехать, лететь is being actually on the way to some place: Мы идём в кино. Мы едем в город. Мы летим в Нью-Йорк. — right now.» — DLI, Lesson 20.  «The verb идти means "to go, be going". It refers to going on foot. This verb belongs to the 1st conjugation (characterized by the vowel -ё-, like живу, -ёшь, -ёт …).» — DLI, Lessons 19–20.  Compare: «Капитан идёт в штаб.» · «Он часто ходит в штаб.» — DLI, Lesson 22. «Мы идём в библиотеку.» (We are headed to the library.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
